content.title: D-dimer use and imaging in suspected pulmonary embolism (PE)

age_adjusted_d_dimer.summary: Specificity of D-dimer for suspected PE decreases with age; age-adjusted cut-offs may improve performance in the elderly.
age_adjusted_d_dimer.age_adjusted_formula: age × 10 µg/L for patients aged >50 years (previously validated)
age_adjusted_d_dimer.follow_up: Patients with a normal age-adjusted D-dimer did not undergo CTPA and were followed for 3 months.
age_adjusted_d_dimer.impact: Use of age-adjusted instead of fixed 500 µg/L D-dimer increased the number of patients in whom PE could be excluded from 6.4% to 30% without additional false-negative findings.

exclusion_criteria: Patients without clinical items and D-dimer < 1000 ng/mL
Patients with one or more clinical items and D-dimer < 500 ng/mL

study_results.ctpa_avoidance_using_algorithm: 48% (compared to 34% if using Wells rule plus fixed 500 ng/mL threshold)

point_of_care_d_dimer_assays.use_case: Community/primary care or remote settings where central lab access is limited
point_of_care_d_dimer_assays.advantages: May avoid referral to central lab and expedite care
point_of_care_d_dimer_assays.limitations: Lower sensitivity and negative predictive value compared with laboratory-based D-dimer tests
point_of_care_d_dimer_assays.recommendation: Point-of-care D-dimer assays should only be used in patients with low pre-test probability.
point_of_care_d_dimer_assays.performance_example: In these situations, PE could be ruled out in 46% of patients with suspected PE without imaging (failure rate 1.5%).

computed_tomographic_pulmonary_angiograp.role: Method of choice for imaging pulmonary vasculature in suspected PE
computed_tomographic_pulmonary_angiograp.capability: Visualization of pulmonary arteries down to subsegmental level

references_mentioned: multinational prospective management study (cohort of 3346 patients)
prospective management trial using Wells-based rule
systematic review and meta-analysis on point-of-care D-dimer assays
